new_mixed_main_proposal.protected_work: Execute a supplied geometry-to-input-power model and multi-body sensible energy balance at a common endpoint, then verify net energy.
new_mixed_main_proposal.predict: Predict whether changing resistance alone determines the time to heat both liquid and vessel.
new_mixed_main_proposal.attempt: EXTENSION. A virtual heater draws 120 W at fixed voltage. A replacement conductor has twice the original diameter and three times its length at unchanged voltage and material. A liquid of capacity 500 J/K and vessel of capacity 100 J/K both start at 20 °C and must reach 35 °C without phase change. Constant loss is 10 W in either trial. Use R proportional to length/area and P=V²/R. Compare the original and replacement heating times and verify the energy balance.
new_mixed_main_proposal.reconstruct: R ratio3/4; new input160 W. Required energy(500+100)×15=9000 J. Original net110 W, time900/11 s≈81.818; new net150 W, time60 s. Ratio11/15. Multiply each net power by time to check9000 J.
new_mixed_main_proposal.diagnose: Identify whether you omitted vessel capacity, used diameter instead of area, or compared input rather than useful power.
new_mixed_main_proposal.repair: Write geometry ratio, electrical input and signed thermal-energy budget separately; verify both net energy products.
new_mixed_main_proposal.boundary_test: If the replacement instead holds original current fixed, what is its time under the same loss and endpoint?
new_mixed_main_proposal.boundary_response_criterion: New input90 W; net80 W; t=112.5 s.
